summary: Import-time dropper fetches and executes opaque binary from attacker-controlled infrastructure
details: On require(), _bootstrap.js selects a platform-specific path, fetches a binary from one of three hardcoded *.workers.dev hosts (oob-worker.cf103-070.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf101-adf.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf99-9b3.workers.dev) with a DNS TXT-record fallback channel over *.dl.wel1.ru subdomains, writes it to /tmp or %TEMP% under a disguised name (.cache_<tag> / dotnet_diag_<tag>.exe), chmods 0755, and detached-spawns it via /bin/sh -c or cmd /c start (_bootstrap.js line 119, 121, 125). Destination hostnames are split across array joins to evade static string search, and a secondary loader reassembles a base64 payload from indexed DNS TXT records (count from c.<domain>, chunks from <i>.<domain>). Cover-story comments frame the behavior as analytics/telemetry.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
